Subject: CAIQ items - end-to-end key lifecycle and operator attestations

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the CAIQ kickoff yesterday. SolsticeFX's audit team is consolidating evidence and asked specifically for: an end-to-end diagram showing where tenant keys are created, wrapped, stored, and evicted; an operator responsibility matrix (who can perform key unwrap/rotation on which systems); and examples of ephemeral key lineage (session keys issued for inference workloads).

Can you provide a single artifact (or small set) that maps the full lifecycle for our tenant and includes an operator sign-off (name + role + date) for the HSM/KMS actions? The auditor prefers CSV or PDF with signatures so they can ingest into their tracker.

Additionally, they asked for a short summary of how in-transit vs at-rest wrapping is handled for tenant BYOK vs Redwood-managed keys. A couple of bullets are fine.

Target due date: EOD May 2 (auditor has a gate on May 6). Let me know if that timeline works.

Best,
Elena Park
Head of Compliance, SolsticeFX

Thanks for the plan. A few clarifications from the auditor side — please include: 

1) HSM attestation: hardware model, firmware version, attestation statement (PKCS#7 or vendor-signed attestation) used for key import. We prefer a vendor attestation PDF or an HSM serial + cert chain.
2) Key wrap chain: show whether tenant BYOK is wrapped locally before transit or whether the tenant key material is imported into our HSM (we need the exact wall-of-words describing the wrap/unwrap sequence).
3) Sample logs: for the wrap/unwrap manifest include the event_id, time (UTC), operator_id (redacted), operation (wrap/unwrap/rotate), and artifact_hash (SHA256). Redaction allowed but timestamps and op types must remain intact.
4) Ephemeral session keys: what TTL and entropy source are used; if derivation uses HKDF/salted HMAC, include algorithm names and parameter sizes (OK to redact secret scalars).

If you can provide the HSM attestation and a sample of 10 wrap/unwrap events in the manifest by EOD May 2, we can keep the audit on schedule.

Marco Bryson
Senior Auditor, Bryson Assurance

Marco / Elena —

Attached are the final artifacts for SolsticeFX (packaged per your request):

- solsticefx_keyflow_map_v1.pdf (diagram, narrative, and explicit wrap/unwrap sequence)
- operator_responsibility_matrix_signed.csv (SSO-attested signatures; last column contains SAML thumbprints; we also included a signer-pdf for three operators)
- wrap-unwrap-log-manifest.sha256 (text file with SHA256 of the 30-day sampled, redacted CSV; individual sample entries included in a separate redacted CSV)
- hsm_attestation_bosch-hsm-2109.pdf (vendor-signed attestation with model and firmware)
- short_summary_BYOK_vs_Redwood.txt (3 bullets explaining transit vs at-rest handling and TTL defaults for ephemeral keys)

Quick notes:
- BYOK: tenant-provided key material is imported into a tenant-segregated HSM partition under a wrapping KEK generated by Redwood; import uses vendor PKCS#11 import mechanism and is recorded in the HSM audit log.
- Redwood-managed keys: generated inside the HSM and never exported; wrapped with a cluster KEK for archival transport.
- Ephemeral session keys: derived via HKDF-SHA256 with per-request nonces; default TTL 30s for streaming inference sessions and 5 minutes for batch jobs (configurable per route). Entropy source: HSM DRBG (NIST SP800-90A compliant).

Links: evidence bundle on Redwood Drive — https://drive.redwood.com/shared/solsticefx/kms-artifacts/INDEX (includes signed CSVs and vendor attestation).

Please reply with confirmation that the artifacts meet the auditor's ingestion requirements. Happy to schedule a 30-minute walkthrough if helpful.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Security & Compliance Lead, Redwood Inference
